# Configuration reference

Tessera reads its settings from `~/Library/Application Support/Tessera/config.toml`, or from `config.toml` in the directory the `TESSERA_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable names (unset by default; for tests and side-by-side installs). Starting Tessera writes no configuration there: without the file the defaults apply, and the file is written, with every default commented, only when the app is asked to open it for editing (a file you create yourself is picked up within a few seconds and never replaced). Saved edits of the file, and of the theme file in use under `themes/`, apply to every open window at once. Every key is optional: a missing key takes the default listed here, and a missing table takes the defaults of all its keys. Unknown keys produce a warning and are kept. A file that does not parse never stops Tessera: the error is reported, and until the file is fixed the defaults apply at launch (with `clipboard_write` off, since the file may turn it off) and the last good configuration stays in effect while running.

Defaults are written as TOML values; *unset* means the key is absent unless you set it.

## Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keys` | table of string | `{}` | Key bindings: each entry maps a chord to a command, so `"cmd+shift+d" = "split_down"` (always quote the chord). An entry adds its chord to the command, ahead of its defaults: the menu item shows the first, the others stay as hidden shortcuts. An entry on another command's default chord takes it from that command; write `"cmd+t" = "unbound"` to drop a default.<br><br>A chord is zero or more modifiers and one key joined by `+`, with no spaces: modifiers `cmd` (`command`, `super`), `ctrl` (`control`), `alt` (`opt`, `option`) and `shift`, in any order and any case; the key is one lowercase character (`t`, `1`, `,`, `ö`) or a name: `escape`, `enter`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `insert`, `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`, `home`, `end`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `f1` to `f35`, `kp_0` to `kp_9`, `kp_decimal`, `kp_divide`, `kp_multiply`, `kp_subtract`, `kp_add`, `kp_enter`, `kp_equal`, and `plus`, `minus`, `equal`, `comma`, `period`, `slash`, `backslash`, `semicolon`, `apostrophe`, `grave_accent`, `left_bracket`, `right_bracket`. A shifted symbol is shorthand for Shift and its US key: `cmd+?` is `cmd+shift+/`, `cmd+plus` is `cmd+shift+=`. Uppercase keys are an error (write `shift+t`). At most 64 bytes.<br><br>A value is a command name, `send_text:<text>` (bytes written to the shell, with the escapes `\e` `\n` `\r` `\t` `\a` `\b` `\f` `\v` `\\` `\"` `\'`, `\xHH` for a raw byte and `\u{H..}` for a character; at most 4096 bytes, written as is), `unbound` (remove the chord's default) or `none` (swallow the key). Commands: `settings`, `hide`, `hide_others`, `quit`, `new_window`, `new_tab`, `close_tab`, `close_window`, `clear_scrollback`, `copy`, `paste`, `paste_plain`, `select_all`, `font_bigger`, `font_smaller`, `font_reset`, `scroll_to_top`, `scroll_to_bottom`, `scroll_page_up`, `scroll_page_down`, `minimize`, `zoom`, `show_tab_bar`, `tab_previous`, `tab_next`, `move_tab_to_new_window`, `merge_all_windows`, `select_tab:1` to `select_tab:9`, `bring_all_to_front`, `help`, `about`, `show_all`, `split_right`, `split_down`, `focus_pane_left`, `focus_pane_right`, `focus_pane_up`, `focus_pane_down`, `focus_pane_previous`, `focus_pane_next`, `zoom_pane` (show the focused pane alone in its tab, or the whole layout again), `equalize_panes` (give every pane of the tab an equal share), `find`, `find_next` (the match toward older output), `find_previous` (toward newer output), `use_selection_for_find`, `copy_find_matches`, `prompt_previous` and `prompt_next` (the shell's previous or next prompt, by its OSC 133 marks; Page Up or Down when the history holds none), `select_last_output` (select the output of the last finished command), and, for features still to come, `copy_mode`.<br><br>Only chords with `cmd` appear in menus; others work in the terminal only. A malformed entry, an unknown command or a chord already bound by an earlier entry is ignored with a warning (the first entry wins); at most 512 entries are read. |

## `[appearance]`

Default appearance; profiles may override.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blur` | boolean | `false` | Background blur behind each pane whose background is translucent (`opacity` below 1.0, or a theme background with alpha). Off while the system's Reduce Transparency setting is on. |
| `cursor_blink` | boolean | `false` | Whether the cursor blinks, unless a program says otherwise (as for `cursor_shape`). tmux and vim turn blinking off on their own (`CSI ? 12 l`), so inside a running tmux a blinking cursor stays off until this is next changed. Changing it applies to open tabs, also where a program turned blinking on or off, but a program still running, such as tmux, may turn it off again. Recorded only for now: the cursor is drawn steady. A value that is not `true` or `false` is reported with a warning and the default is used. |
| `cursor_shape` | one of `"block"`, `"underline"`, `"beam"` | `"block"` | The cursor's shape: `"block"`, `"underline"` or `"beam"` (a vertical bar), exactly as written here. A program may change it (DECSCUSR, `CSI Ps SP q`, as vim and fish do); it returns to this one when the program asks for the default or resets the terminal. Any other value is reported with a warning and the default is used. |
| `dim_inactive_panes` | float | `0.0` | How much to darken the panes of a split tab that do not have the keyboard focus, from 0.0 (off) to 0.8, drawn as a black overlay of that opacity. A tab with one pane is never dimmed. A value outside the range is clamped (not a number means 0.0) with a warning. Applies to open windows when the file changes. Set it here only: in a profile's `appearance` it is ignored with a warning, since the window, not the session, draws it. |
| `font_family` | string | `"Menlo"` | Font family. |
| `font_size` | float | `13.0` | Font size in points, clamped on load to `4.0`..=`512.0`. |
| `opacity` | float | `1.0` | Background opacity, 0.0..=1.0. A window is translucent while any pane of its tab is. The system's Reduce Transparency setting draws every session opaque. |
| `theme` | string | `"Tessera Dark"` | Colour theme, by name. Looked up first among the `*.toml` files in `themes/` next to this file (by file stem, then by the `name` key inside each file), then among the bundled themes: Tessera Dark, Tessera Light, Solarized Dark, Solarized Light, Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox Dark, One Dark, Tokyo Night and Catppuccin Mocha. Names match ignoring case, and any run of characters other than letters and digits counts as one separator, with `+` read as the word `plus`: `solarized-dark` and `SOLARIZED DARK` are Solarized Dark, `Dracula+` is `dracula-plus`, not Dracula, but `solarizeddark` is not Solarized Dark. A user file shadows a bundled theme of the same name. Unicode is not normalised, so an accented name matches only when typed in the same form (precomposed or combining) as the theme's. An unknown name falls back to Tessera Dark with a warning. |

## `[general]`

Application-wide settings.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confirm_close` | boolean | `true` | Confirm before closing a window with running jobs. |
| `default_profile` | string | `"Default"` | The `[[profiles]]` entry new tabs, windows and panes use when none is chosen (a pane split off another uses that pane's). When no profile has this name, the built-in one is used: `[appearance]` and the login shell (with a warning, unless the name is `"Default"`). |

## `[plugins]`

Plugin enablement, keyed by plugin id.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | array of string | `[]` | Plugin ids that are enabled. |

## `[[profiles]]`

Named profiles.

An array of tables: write one `[[profiles]]` block per entry. Default: `[]`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appearance` | table, optional | *unset* | Appearance for this profile's sessions: each key set here replaces the one in `[appearance]`, each key left out follows `[appearance]` (also when it changes). In 0.1.0 a key left out here was reset to its built-in default instead (a profile that set only `font_size` also reset `theme`, `opacity` and the cursor). `dim_inactive_panes` cannot be set here (the window draws it): it is ignored with a warning. See [`[profiles.appearance]`](#profilesappearance). |
| `command` | string, optional | *unset* | Command to run instead of the login shell: one program name or path runs directly (`"/opt/homebrew/bin/fish"`), anything with a space runs through `/bin/sh -c` (`"ssh build-box"`). Unset means the login shell. |
| `name` | string | `"Default"` | Display name, shown in the menus. Should be unique: of two profiles with one name, the first is used and the second is reported with a warning. |
| `working_directory` | string, optional | *unset* | Starting directory; `~` at the start is your home directory. A directory that does not exist falls back to your home directory with a warning. Used only when the session is not given a directory of its own; unset means your home directory. |

### `[profiles.appearance]`

Appearance for this profile's sessions: each key set here replaces the one in `[appearance]`, each key left out follows `[appearance]` (also when it changes). In 0.1.0 a key left out here was reset to its built-in default instead (a profile that set only `font_size` also reset `theme`, `opacity` and the cursor). `dim_inactive_panes` cannot be set here (the window draws it): it is ignored with a warning.

Optional table; *unset* by default. It belongs to the `[[profiles]]` entry it follows.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blur` | boolean, optional | *unset* | Background blur behind each of this profile's panes whose background is translucent (`opacity` below 1.0, or a theme background with alpha). |
| `cursor_blink` | boolean, optional | *unset* | Whether the cursor blinks, as for `[appearance] cursor_blink`. A value that is not `true` or `false` is reported with a warning and `[appearance]`'s value is used. |
| `cursor_shape` | one of `"block"`, `"underline"`, `"beam"` | *unset* | The cursor's shape, `"block"`, `"underline"` or `"beam"`, as for `[appearance] cursor_shape`. Any other value is reported with a warning and `[appearance]`'s shape is used. |
| `font_family` | string, optional | *unset* | Font family. Not honoured per profile yet: the font is shared by every session, so only `[appearance] font_family` changes it. |
| `font_size` | float, optional | *unset* | Font size in points, clamped on load as for `[appearance] font_size`. |
| `opacity` | float, optional | *unset* | Background opacity of this profile's sessions, 0.0..=1.0. A window is translucent while any pane of its tab is, and stays opaque only while every one is; an opaque session still draws its own opaque background. The system's Reduce Transparency setting draws every session opaque. |
| `theme` | string, optional | *unset* | Colour theme, by name, looked up as for `[appearance] theme`. |

## `[terminal]`

Terminal emulation limits and shell integration.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clipboard_write` | boolean | `true` | Whether programs may write the clipboard (OSC 52, as tmux and Neovim do over `ssh`): up to 1 MiB of text per write. Programs can never read the clipboard. A value that is not `true` or `false` is reported with a warning and counts as `false`: writes are refused until it is fixed. When Tessera starts with a `config.toml` that does not load at all (a syntax error anywhere in it, such as `clipboard_write = off` without quotes, a duplicate key, a file that is not UTF-8, or a `config.toml` symlink whose target is missing), writes are refused as well until the file is fixed, while the other defaults apply; emptying the file does not turn them back on (a save that truncates first leaves it empty for a moment), only a version of it with something in it that loads. Applies to every session at once when changed. |
| `scrollback_lines` | integer | `10000` | Maximum number of scrollback lines kept per pane. Applies to sessions started after a change; running sessions keep the size they started with. Large values cost time on every width change: resizing a window re-wraps the whole history while the terminal is locked, about 0.2 ms per 1,000 lines (1-4 ms at 10,000 lines, 14-41 ms at 100,000), so at the 10,000,000 limit a full history takes about 18 GB of memory and each resize stalls the pane for 2-4 seconds. |
| `shell_integration` | one of `"auto"`, `"off"` | `"auto"` | Shell integration for zsh and fish (bash support is to follow): `"auto"` makes the shells Tessera starts load its scripts, which mark prompts and commands and report the working directory; `"off"` starts them unchanged. A session started with `TESSERA_SHELL_INTEGRATION` in its environment is never changed. |
